words.gloss: saying that / that which is called
is of the measure of the guest's worth

literal: There is no such thing as saying 'the benefit is of this much measure'; the benefit of the sacrifice of hospitality is of the measure of the guest's own worth.
translation: There is no fixed measure for the benefit of hosting a guest; its true measure is the worth of the guest who is received.
modern: "விருந்தினரை உபசரிப்பதால் கிடைக்கும் நன்மை இவ்வளவுதான்" என்று வரையறுத்துக் கூற முடியாது; அந்த விருந்தினரின் தகுதியே அந்த உபசரிப்பாகிய வேள்வியின் பயனின் அளவாகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that the spiritual and moral reward of hospitality cannot be measured by a fixed material standard, such as the cost of the food served. Instead, the true value of the act is determined by the character and qualities of the guest who receives it. The poet uses the word 'வேள்வி' (sacrifice) to describe the noble duty of hosting, elevating it to a sacred ritual. The word 'துணை' is repeated to emphasize that the measure of the reward matches the measure of the guest's worth.
